monument_name: Devala Divyapura, śikhara temple 4 (from approx. 8th-10th century)
description_en: A freestanding Shaiva śikhara temple from approx. 8th-10th century.The monument is part of a complex comprising five similar temples distributed accross a longitudinal platform oriented south-north. This platform, also known locally as Dewal Park, is located in the locality of Dewal Divyapur, 3 km west of Chipur and a dozen km north-west of Amargadhi, the district headquarters. The temples were seemingly all dedicated to Shaiva cult, as indicated by the presence ofjalaharīin the sanctums and oneśivaliṅga, placed, in 2014, in the sanctum of Temple 4.Temple 4 is freestanding, north of temples 1, 2 and 3, and south of temple 5. It is oriented to the east. It is composed of a single sanctum (Skt.garbhagṛha). The sanctum is preceded by a short vestibule (Skt.antarāla). The nearby temples 1 and 2 (DDL0250andDDL0251) were most likely provided the same feature (now missing). Inside the sanctum is a stone image of Gaṇeśa and a stoneśivaliṅga. The south, west and north façades of the monument have carved niches (Skt.rathikā). The upper plinth of the temple's exterior walls is decorated with (eroded) decorative and floral motifs. On top of the tower is a large, half-broken stoneāmalakadisc. This is the largest monument in Devala Divyapura.These architectural features evoke temples built in Uttarakhand (India) around the 7th-8th century, and especially Temples 1 and 2 in Jageshwar (seeChanchani 2019, 81-83, fig. 3.7.). It may thus be suggested that this monument, as well as the four others found at the site, was built between the 8th and 10th century (Andolfatto 2022, 38;Sharma 2012, 284). This relative dating places the temples amongst the oldest known form of architecture in west Nepal.
identified_threats: Other, Missing stones at plinths, Erosion
